s.t: Esmeray’s song began in Italy as ‘Jesahel’, first sung by the band Delirium at the 1972 Sanremo festival; she recorded it in 1974 with Turkish words by Oktay Yurdatapan.
s.src: The Ringo Jets ve Hey! Douglas'dan Esmeray'a saygı duruşu (Dergy, 8 December 2020)
s.q: Delirium adlı İtalyan grup tarafından “Jesahel” ismiyle 1972 Sanremo Müzik Festivali’nde ilk defa seslendirilen şarkı, ülkemizin kült sahne ve ses sanatçılarından Esmeray tarafından 1974 yılında Oktay Yurdatapan’ın yazdığı Türkçe sözlerle kaydedildi.

s.t: Delirium’s ‘Jesahel’, the Italian original, was covered by Shirley Bassey as ‘Jezahel’ in 1972; Public Enemy sampled its horns for ‘Harder Than You Think’, Channel 4’s Paralympics theme since 2012.
s.q: It borrows from Shirley Bassey's 1972 track "Jezahel", a cover of the song "Jesahel" by the Italian prog rock band Delirium. ... its use as Channel 4's theme for their coverage of the Paralympic Games since the 2012 Summer Paralympics ... uses a horn sample from Shirley Bassey's 'Jezahel'

s.t: Esmeray’s recording was the B-side of ‘Unutama Beni’, her most popular single, but over the years it became a classic with a loyal following of its own.
s.src: The Ringo Jets ve Hey! Douglas'dan Esmeray'a saygı duruşu (Dergy, 8 December 2020)
s.q: Bu kayıt, sanatçının en popüler teklisi olan “Unutama Beni” 45’liğinin B yüzünde yer aldı ve yıllar içerisinde kendi sadık dinleyici kitlesini yaratmış bir repertuvar klasiğine dönüştü.

f.t: Kept off TRT’s radio and television, she named her 1975 album Yayınlanamaz (‘Cannot be broadcast’), its back cover telling TRT it had no right to decide for the people.
f.src: Mert Dirim, ‘Çikolata renkli şarkıcısı Esmeray’ (Yeni Asır, 2 March 2024)
f.q: Esmeray şarkıları bir türlü TRT engelini aşıp televizyon ve radyodan dinleyiciye ulaşamamaktadır. Esmeray bu durumu 1975 yılında yayımlanan albümüne "Yayınlanamaz" adını vererek protesto eder. ... "Sizin halk adına böyle bir karar vermeye yetkiniz yoktur. Bu hak yalnızca halka aittir."

f.t: Her husband Şemi Diriker’s ‘Unutama Beni’ won TRT’s 1974 Toplu İğne contest for her, yet the broadcaster soon censored it, seeing its Arabic maqam sound as foreign.
f.src: Kornelia Binicewicz, ‘Esmeray: the untold story of an Afro-Turk music star’ (The National, 22 March 2016)
f.q: The song Unutama Beni (Do Not Forget Me) was written by her husband and artistic partner, Semi Diriker, and was chosen by the audience as the best song ... The deep sound of the song was based on Arabic maqam ... But soon after its victory, it was censored by the channel. Arabic influences ... were now perceived as symbols of a foreign culture.

f.t: Her song ‘13,5’ is named after an old Turkish superstition: that you should pinch yourself whenever you see someone with dark skin.
f.src: Discovering the women singers of Turkey from the 70s and 80s (The Attic)
f.q: the song is addressing an old prejudice towards dark-skinned persons in Turkey ... The superstition, which is referred to as “13,5”, suggests that you should pinch yourself whenever you see someone with a dark skin.

f.t: Her first record, in 1974, didn’t carry her name, as she sang for the studio group Kim Bunlar; soon after, a 45 bore it, and the whole country knew her.
f.src: Mert Dirim, ‘Çikolata renkli şarkıcısı Esmeray’ (Yeni Asır, 2 March 2024)
f.q: Üzerinde adı olmasa da ilk plağı o yıl yayınlanır. Şat Yapım projesi olan Kim Bunlar grubunun solisti olarak girer stüdyoya... Hemen sonra yayınlanan 45'lik plağın kapağında bu defa adı yazmaktadır ve tüm ülke onu tanımaktadır.

nf.t: Its Italian original, via Shirley Bassey, ended up in Channel 4’s Paralympics theme
nf.q: It borrows from Shirley Bassey's 1972 track "Jezahel", a cover of the song "Jesahel" by the Italian prog rock band Delirium. ... The song is also known in the UK for its use as Channel 4's theme for their coverage of the Paralympic Games since the 2012 Summer Paralympics
